title: True Dual-Port RAM
constraints: 32 × 8-bit memory with two independent read/write ports A and B on one clock. Each port reads every cycle (registered, read-first: the value before this edge's writes).
If both ports write the **same** address on the same edge, port **A** wins.
hints: Two ports in one clocked process: write B first and then A, so A's write wins when the addresses collide.
Both reads use the pre-edge contents, so read before (or independently of) the writes.
In a real FPGA, a same-address write collision is 'undefined'. Specifying a winner makes the model deterministic.

examples.check: port A writes, port B reads
examples.title: cross-port
examples.input: A writes 0x11 to 3, then B reads 3

examples.title: collision
examples.input: A and B both write address 7

examples.title: read-first
